record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of infinite dimensional algebras
record.context_brief: Fraction division algebra from enveloping algebra
record.original_question: Using the same Lie algebra generated by v_1 and v_2 from the self-similar derivation construction over the truncated polynomial algebra T, let U be its universal associative enveloping algebra and let Z be the center of U. Because powers of elements of the Lie algebra fall into Z, form the ring of fractions D = (Z \ {0})^{-1} U. Is D an algebraic division algebra?

evidence.quote: Let U be the universal associative enveloping algebra of Lie <v1, v2>. Let Z be the center of U.
Consider the ring of fractions D = (Z r {0})-1 U. Problem 9. Is D an algebraic division algebra?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let F be a field of characteristic 2 and let
  T = F[t_i : i ≥ 0] / (t_i^2 : i ≥ 0)
be the truncated polynomial algebra in countably many variables. For each i ≥ 0 let ∂_i denote the F-linear derivation of T determined by ∂_i(t_j) = δ_{ij}. Define two derivations of T recursively by the self-similar formulas
  v_1 = ∂_0 + t_1 · v_2',   v_2 = ∂_1 + t_2 · v_1',
where v_1' and v_2' are obtained from v_1 and v_2, respectively, by shifting all indices up by 1 (i.e. by replacing each t_i with t_{i+1} and each ∂_i with ∂_{i+1}). Equivalently, v_1 and v_2 are the unique derivations of T satisfying these self-similar identities.

Let L = ⟨v_1, v_2⟩ be the Lie subalgebra of Der(T) generated by v_1 and v_2 under the commutator bracket. Let U = U(L) be its universal associative enveloping algebra, and let Z denote the center of U. It is known that suitable powers of elements of L lie in Z, so that Z \ {0} is a (left and right) Ore set in U. Form the ring of fractions
  D = (Z \ {0})^{-1} U.

Question: Is D an algebraic division algebra over F? That is, is every nonzero element of D invertible, and is every element of D algebraic over F?
artifact.category_tag: Self-similar Lie algebras and enveloping algebras
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up an explicit resolution of this specific question on the localization D = (Z\{0})^{-1}U of the enveloping algebra of the self-similar Petrogradsky-type Lie algebra ⟨v_1, v_2⟩ being an algebraic division algebra. Related work by Petrogradsky, Shestakov and Zelmanov discusses nil and PI properties of such enveloping algebras, but the algebraicity of D as a division ring does not appear to have been settled in the sources retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Self-similar Lie algebras (Petrogradsky)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses self-similar restricted Lie algebras generated by derivations v_1, v_2 of truncated polynomial algebras in characteristic 2 and properties of their enveloping algebras.
status_evidence.claim: The construction of L = ⟨v_1, v_2⟩ as self-similar derivations of a truncated polynomial algebra is studied, but the algebraicity of the fraction division ring D is not resolved there.

status_evidence.title: Poisson identities of enveloping algebras (Giambruno–Petrogradsky)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies identities of enveloping algebras of self-similar nil Lie algebras, central elements arising from powers of Lie elements.
status_evidence.claim: Centrality of certain powers of elements of L is established, allowing the Ore localization defining D, but D's algebraicity as a division ring is not addressed.
